author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Visitors can narrow the veterinarian list to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces (the paged HTML directory and the reinstated JSON list) accept an optional specialty in the address and return only veterinarians holding it. Matching is whole-name and case-insensitive. The contract is URL-only; no page control is added.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only veterinarians holding that specialty; pagination applies to the narrowed list
[REQ-VET-003] GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns a JSON document containing only veterinarians holding that specialty
[REQ-VET-003] a specialty differing from a held specialty only by letter case matches on both surfaces (e.g. SURGERY matches surgery)
[REQ-VET-003] a prefix of a specialty name matches no veterinarian on either surface (e.g. surg matches nothing)
[REQ-VET-003] a specialty no veterinarian holds yields HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON document and an empty veterinarian list
[REQ-VET-003] an empty or whitespace-only specialty behaves exactly as if the parameter were absent, on both surfaces
[REQ-VET-003] on a narrowed HTML directory spanning several pages, every pagination link (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carries the specialty so the linked page stays narrowed
[REQ-VET-003] a veterinarian holding several specialties appears when any one is named and is still shown with all of them; a veterinarian holding no specialty never appears in a narrowed list
[REQ-VET-004] without the parameter, GET /vets returns every veterinarian with their specialties in one JSON document, as today
[REQ-VET-001] without the parameter, GET /vets.html lists every veterinarian a page at a time, as today
non_goals: any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface (possible follow-up request)
free-text or prefix search for veterinarians (NG-9, narrowed but still in force)
narrowing by more than one specialty at once
any change to either surface's behavior when no specialty is named
new user-facing wording or message keys

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Stays inside the vet feature package on the existing controller-to-repository shape (system-design.md § Overview; ADR 2026-07-31 feature-package organization). Narrowing is a VetRepository query, following the paged derived-query precedent OwnerRepository sets for owner search (grep of OwnerRepository/OwnerController; IDE oracle not connected, so this rests on the weaker grep basis). It comes in paged and unpaged forms, compares whole names case-insensitively, returns each veterinarian at most once, and joins without fetching (system-design.md § Persistence, new paragraph). VetController normalizes the specialty parameter: blank or absent becomes 'not narrowed'. That is binding, not a business rule (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row). The controller then delegates to the narrowed or unnarrowed read on both routes. The HTML route pages over the narrowed list; the JSON route wraps the whole narrowed list in Vets. New ground: narrowed reads bypass the vet cache (new ADR 2026-09-30-narrowed-veterinarian-reads-bypass-the-vet-cache), and § Scale and Load is created with the veterinarian rows. Doc sync done at triage: /vets reinstated as a supported JSON surface under REQ-VET-004 (Overview, Security Context, Contracts rows), the Known Defects row for the unconsumed route removed, and REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004 placed in the Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController and CacheConfiguration Contracts rows. The ADR index gains rows for the PRD expert's non-goal ADR and for the new cache ADR.
integration_points: Binding, GET /vets.html and GET /vets: specialty binds as an optional request-scoped String @RequestParam alongside the existing int page. No persisted type is bound and no new @InitBinder is needed. Only a blank or absent value is normalized, to 'not narrowed'. A non-blank value passes to the query unchanged; do not trim it (surrounding spaces is an open PRD question, left unsettled and untested)

Boundary, repository (matching semantics): real implementation. New VetRepositoryTests uses @DataJpaTest + @AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = Replace.NONE) over the embedded H2 seed data, following ClinicServiceTests. Seed: surgery is held by Linda Douglas and Rafael Ortega; Douglas also holds dentistry; Carter and Jenkins hold none. That covers case-insensitive match, prefix non-match, unknown name returning empty, a multi-specialty veterinarian loaded with all his specialties, and no-specialty exclusion. A small PageRequest proves paging over the narrowed list
Boundary, framework transport: MockMvc in the existing @WebMvcTest VetControllerTests (the sanctioned mock, testing-principles § Mocking Policy)

Boundary, repository behind the controller in VetControllerTests: keep the class's existing @MockitoBean VetRepository fixture as the recorded framework-stub exception. A web slice has no JPA, so the real repository cannot load. The class-wide fixture already occupies the repository bean, so a hand-written double cannot sit beside it. The new tests need only canned returns and argument checks. Controller tests assert only binding and presentation: blank routes to the unnarrowed read, the named specialty reaches the narrowed read, page links carry the specialty, and the JSON shape holds. They never assert matching semantics through the stub

Template: vetList.html page links (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carry the specialty through Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, from a model attribute holding the normalized specialty. Links rendered without a named specialty stay byte-identical to today's
Cache: the narrowed repository reads carry no @Cacheable; the existing unnarrowed reads keep theirs unchanged

patterns.description: paged derived query with a caller-supplied criterion: the shape for the narrowed paged read
existing findPaginated helper and page-size local: narrowed paging reuses it rather than adding a second page size
@DataJpaTest over H2 seed data: the setup VetRepositoryTests copies

risks.risk: The narrowed paged read on the veterinarian directory path (system-design.md § Scale and Load, directory-page row)
risks.mitigation: Page in the database over the narrowed query; the size is bounded, so use the simplest readable form

risks.risk: The narrowed unpaged read on the JSON list path (§ Scale and Load, JSON-list row)
risks.mitigation: One unpaged read, returned whole; bounded by the veterinarian row, so use the simplest readable form

risks.risk: Caching the narrowed reads would let any caller grow the unbounded vet cache with arbitrary specialty text (system-design.md § Threat Model, cache-growth row)

A fetch join, or filtering the loaded collection, would truncate a matched veterinarian's specialties to the named one. That breaks 'still shown with all of them' (system-design.md § Persistence, narrowing paragraph)
risks.mitigation: Use a plain, non-fetch join (a derived query does this). The EAGER mapping then loads the full set by secondary select. VetRepositoryTests asserts that Linda Douglas, matched by surgery, still holds dentistry

risks.risk: Duplicate rows: the H2 vet_specialties table has no unique constraint, and specialty names are not unique case-insensitively, so a join can return a veterinarian twice (system-design.md § Persistence, 'appears at most once')
risks.mitigation: Use a distinct query (e.g. a findDistinctBy... derived query), which also yields a distinct count for paging

risks.risk: Template expression injection or XSS if the specialty is spliced into a link through __${...}__ preprocessing or string concatenation (security-principles.md § Realization, Injection and Cross-site scripting rows; system-design.md § Threat Model, XSS row)
risks.mitigation: Pass the specialty only as a link-expression parameter, which URL-encodes it. Never preprocess or concatenate it into an expression

risks.risk: Case-insensitive whole-name matching can diverge across H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, as owner search already does on PostgreSQL (system-design.md § Known Defects, first row)
risks.mitigation: Express case-insensitivity in the query itself (derived IgnoreCase, which applies UPPER on both sides) rather than relying on column collation

risks.risk: A null-valued Thymeleaf link parameter renders as a bare name, so unnarrowed links gain '&specialty'. That changes the unnarrowed surface, a PRD non-goal
risks.mitigation: Guard the parameter so unnarrowed links render exactly as today; a VetControllerTests assertion on an unnarrowed multi-page link pins it

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log. Dispatch-start correction: line 4 anchored to line 2 by mistake; line 5 re-anchors this dispatch to the prd-entry at line 3. Brief gaps for the owner of docs/security-principles.md, which is outside this agent's write scope: its § Realization table has no row for request-derived values keying an unbounded cache, and none for template-expression injection through Thymeleaf preprocessing. This slice's risks cite the nearest rows (Injection, Cross-site scripting) plus the system-design Threat Model rows. Test names come from the prd-entry; the matching-semantics names (theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchTheWholeNameIgnoringCase, theSpecialtyFilterShouldYieldAnEmptyVetListWhenNoVetHoldsTheSpecialty) belong in VetRepositoryTests. The PRD's open questions (surrounding spaces, repeated parameter, a narrowed-state indicator) stay undecided in design and must not be pinned by tests.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Fix delta (changeset --base-tree 5931e4ce) moves the specialty into the pagination link base at vetList.html:28 `th:with="pageLinkBase=${namedSpecialty == null} ? '/vets.html' : '/vets.html?specialty=' + ${#uris.escapeQueryParam(namedSpecialty)}"`. The request value is query-param-escaped before concatenation, so '&', '=', '#' and '%' cannot inject extra parameters or a fragment. The base always begins with the fixed literal '/vets.html', so the caller cannot turn the href into an absolute, javascript: or data: URL. th:href attribute-escapes the rendered link. The value is concatenated as data inside a standard expression, never evaluated as an expression, and no `__${` preprocessing or th:utext appears in the added lines (grep -F over the changeset '+' lines returned none).

The encoding claim is exercised: VetControllerTests.java:65 `URL_ENCODED_SPECIALTY_WITH_RESERVED_CHARACTERS = "ear%20%26%20nose"` is asserted in a rendered page link at line 177, and the build-pass (line 19) records the test run green.

This dispatch completes the second half of the checklist that the round-1 truncation deferred. Credential sweep: grep -i for password|secret|token|apikey|credential|private.?key over the changeset '+' lines hit only docs/system-design.md prose describing environment-supplied datasource credentials; no secret appears in the diff. Error handling: the new code adds no catch blocks and no exception text reaches the response. An unknown specialty yields an empty list, and page<1 keeps the pre-existing PageRequest.of behavior (VetController.java:64 `Pageable pageable = PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize);`), which this change leaves untouched. Resource management: the paged route reads a fixed page size of 5, and the unpaged narrowed /vets read is bounded by the vet table exactly as the existing findAll() is. Narrowed queries stay uncached (VetRepository javadoc), so input cannot grow the vets cache.
